description: Installation of children's play area and associated works (RETROSPECTIVE)
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and documents:Location PlanPre-existing Site Plan - ELC- LGA- 00- XX- DR- A- 0101Existing Site Plan - EC-06-2026 - PL01Proposed Site Plan - EC-06-2026 - PL03Proposed Elevations - EC-06-2026 - PL04Supporting Information: 	Arboricultural Method StatementArboricultural Impact AssessmentHeritage StatementCovering LetterReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.
The development shall be implemented in accordance with the materials indicated on the plans/application formReason: To preserve the character of the Conservation Area.

Prior to the commencement of the works hereby approved (including all preparatory work), a scheme for remedial works to the rooting environment of the lime tree shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall be prepared by a qualified arboricultural consultant and shall include details of:- Methodology and specification for the restoration of ground levels to those prior to the installation of the block paving, using suitable soil and amelioration as required.- Methodology and specification for any other improvements required to the rooting zone of the lime tree, following assessment of the rooting area, which would be of benefit to the tree following the invasive works it has suffered to its roots and rooting environment, as well as benefit it's general vitality e.g. - aeration/decompaction, mulching, nutrient addition, fencing off of RPA (i.e. chestnut pale fencing) etc.Reason - to ensure that the long-term health and benefit of a high quality tree of significant amenity is maintained and preserved following adverse works and unsympathetic hard surface installation within its rooting environment.

Throughout the implementation of the approved scheme the following consideration of the trees must be given.A. No equipment, machinery or materials are to be brought on the site for the purpose of the development until all the trees to be retained have been protected in accordance with section 6.2 of British Standard 5837:2012 Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction -recommendations throughout the implementation of the scheme.B. No fire shall be lit within 10m from the outside of the crown spread of the trees to be retained.C. The ground levels within the protected areas shall not be altered, nor shall any excavation be made, without the written consent of the local planning authority.D. No mixing of cement or use of other materials or substances to take place within a Root Protection Area (RPA), or close enough to a RPA whereby seepage or displacement of those materials or substances could enter a RPA.Reason: To ensure that the tree (s) are not damaged or otherwise adversely affected by building operations and soil compaction.
